item.title: Qiskit MCP Servers
item.description:
Production-ready Model Context Protocol servers that give AI assistants direct access to quantum computing infrastructure. Built on FastMCP with async-first architecture, full type safety, and 65%+ test coverage.

Five specialized servers:

  • Qiskit Server — Circuit creation, manipulation, and transpilation
  • Code Assistant Server — AI-assisted quantum programming via Granite models
  • IBM Runtime Server — Hardware access, job execution, and backend selection
  • AI Transpiler Server — RL-powered circuit optimization
  • Qiskit Gym Server — Lets AI agents train RL models for circuit synthesis on their own: create environments, launch PPO or AlphaZero training, and synthesize circuits ( )

Enables AI systems to autonomously generate quantum code, select optimal backends, execute circuits on real hardware, train their own circuit-synthesis models, and provide expert quantum computing guidance—all through a standardized protocol.

item.title: IBM Quantum Lab
item.description:
Led development of IBM Quantum Lab, the cloud notebook environment where IBM Quantum users wrote and ran Qiskit code against real quantum hardware without installing anything. Built as a JupyterHub deployment on Kubernetes integrated with the IBM Quantum platform, open to ~240,000 enrolled users.

Engineering challenges solved:

  • Custom authentication against the IBM Quantum platform
  • Persistent per-user storage and tailored user environments with Qiskit and tutorials pre-installed
  • Automatic selection of hardware resources for different user profiles
  • Abuse protection and performance at scale — peaks of ~800 concurrent user servers during the IBM Quantum Challenge

Presented at JupyterCon 2020.
